## Natural history notes

A medium-sized flower scarab characterized by a dark brown to black, somewhat velvety body with pale speckling or mottling and a compact oval shape. In Florida, the Dark Flower Scarab is found in fields, gardens, roadsides, pine flatwoods, forest edges, parks, and yards where flowers, fruiting plants, and decaying organic matter are available. Adults visit flowers and may feed on pollen, nectar, fruit, or sap, while the larvae develop in soil or decaying organic material, helping recycle nutrients and serving as prey for birds, mammals, and other insect-eating animals.
